result.label: Source-read

claims.claim: An acknowledgment or promise is insufficient evidence of a new or continuing contract to take the case outside the time-limit statutes unless it is in a writing signed by the party to be charged.
claims.quote: No acknowledgment or promise is sufficient evidence of a new or continuing contract, by which to take the case out of the operation of this title, unless the same is contained in some writing, signed by the party to be charged thereby
claims.note: This states a necessary condition, not that signing any writing restarts the period. The draft separately states the payment exception.

claims.claim: A payment of principal or interest on a promissory note by the party to be charged counts as an acknowledgment or promise of a continuing contract.
claims.quote: any payment on account of principal or interest due on a promissory note made by the party to be charged shall be deemed a sufficient acknowledgment or promise of a continuing contract
claims.note: The claim is limited to promissory notes, not payments on every written debt.

claims.claim: Each such payment stops the running of the time to sue on the note.
claims.quote: to stop, from time to time as any such payment is made, the running of the time within which an action may be commenced upon the principal sum or upon any installment of principal or interest due on such note
claims.note: The statute covers actions for principal or for installments of principal or interest.

claims.claim: Each such payment starts a new period.
claims.quote: and to start the running of a new period of time
claims.note: Subject to the already-barred limitation stated next.

claims.claim: No such payment by itself revives an already-barred cause of action.
claims.quote: but no such payment of itself shall revive a cause of action once barred.

claims.claim: The limitations period for an action on a contract, obligation or liability founded on a written instrument is four years within the stated scope.
claims.quote:
Within four years:
(a) An action upon any contract, obligation or liability founded upon an instrument in writing, except as provided in Section 336a;
claims.note: The post-sale money-judgment proviso is outside the stated scope.

claims.claim: The written-instrument rule is subject to the Section 336a exception.
claims.note: The draft identifies the exception without claiming what Section 336a provides.

claims.claim: Once the Section 337 period has run, a person may not sue to collect the debt.
claims.quote: When the period in which an action must be commenced under this section has run, a person shall not bring suit or initiate an arbitration or other legal proceeding to collect the debt.
claims.note: The prohibition is tied to expiration of the period.

claims.claim: Once that period has run, a person may not start arbitration or another legal proceeding to collect the debt.
claims.quote: When the period in which an action must be commenced under this section has run, a person shall not bring suit or initiate an arbitration or other legal proceeding to collect the debt.
claims.note: The claim concerns initiating proceedings to collect the debt.

claims.claim: The Section 337 period may be extended only under Section 360.
claims.quote: The period in which an action may be commenced under this section shall only be extended pursuant to Section 360.

result.summary: The provided statutes support each claim within the stated unsecured-debt scope. The draft distinguishes a qualifying note payment before expiration from a payment made after the claim is already barred.
